vt10_ambrosiano.topic: Sindona, Marcinkus, Banco Ambrosiano collapse, Calvi's death, 1984 settlement, 1987 warrant

claims.text: Calvi became general manager of Banco Ambrosiano in 1971 and chairman in 1975; in 1981 he received a four-year suspended sentence and a $19.8m fine for moving $27m out of Italy; he left Rome on 10 June 1982 on a false passport; a postal clerk found his body at 7:30 am on 18 June 1982 hanging from scaffolding under Blackfriars Bridge, with five bricks and about $14,000 in his pockets

First London inquest (July 1982): suicide; second inquest (July 1983): open verdict; body exhumed December 1998; City of London Police reopened as murder inquiry September 2003; Rome trial opened 5 October 2005 against Calò, Carboni, Kleinszig, Diotallevi, Vittor; all acquitted 6 June 2007 for insufficient evidence; acquittals confirmed on appeal 7 May 2010 and by Cassation 18 November 2011

In 1982 Banco Ambrosiano could not account for $1.287bn; the Bank of Italy took over; Nuovo Banco Ambrosiano replaced it in August 1982 under Giovanni Bazoli; IOR was the main shareholder; Marcinkus had been a director of Ambrosiano Overseas (Nassau); Gelli's 12-year sentence for the crash confirmed by Cassation April 1998

TIME (21 May 1984): the Vatican agreed to pay $244m to Ambrosiano's 120 bank creditors 'solely because of moral considerations'; the Church 'has always insisted that it has no legal or financial responsibility'; $1.3bn missing-funds scandal

CSM (22 May 1984): tentative accord for $250m; Vatican officials denied wrongdoing and said they were victims of a 'hidden project' by Calvi; collapse stemmed from about $1.3bn in loans to Panamanian companies nominally owned by the Vatican bank

Avvenire/Anfossi: Geneva agreement 25 May 1984; IOR paid $250m as a 'contributo volontario' without admitting responsibility; Andreatta had demanded $1,159m calling IOR a 'de facto partner'; mixed Italian-Vatican commission split in autumn 1983; Marcinkus said the letters of patronage were issued to curb further debts and Calvi used them otherwise
Other figures for the 1984 payment: $224m (Wikipedia IOR/Calvi) and $241m (SAGE encyclopedia); SAGE: the Vatican sent letters reassuring creditors

Arrest warrant of 20 February 1987 by the Milan examining magistrate against Marcinkus, Luigi Mennini and Pellegrino De Strobel for 'concorso in bancarotta fraudolenta'; Court of Cassation (17 July 1987, n. 3932) annulled the order confirming it and held Italian courts lacked jurisdiction under Lateran Treaty Art. 11; Constitutional Court 609/1988 (6 June 1988) declared questions on Art. 11 inadmissible

Marcinkus headed the IOR 1971-1989, resigned from Vatican service 30 October 1990, died in Sun City, Arizona, 20 February 2006; said Calvi had released him in writing from liabilities under the letters; in 1990: 'I have never done anything wrong'

Sindona: association with the Vatican bank from 1969; Franklin National declared insolvent 8 October 1974; liquidator Giorgio Ambrosoli murdered 11 July 1979; US conviction 1980 on 65 counts, 25 years; extradited 25 September 1984; 12 years for Banca Privata Italiana bankruptcy 16 March 1985; life for instigating Ambrosoli murder 18 March 1986; died of cyanide 22 March 1986
IOR losses from Sindona's collapse estimated by one source at 35 billion lire; Holy See hired Sindona after losing its Italian tax exemption on investment income in 1968

vt10_later_cases.topic: IOR and APSA cases 2010-2021: 2010 seizure, Scarano, Caloia/Liuzzo

claims.text: 21 September 2010: Italian authorities seized about 23m euros of the IOR's deposit at Credito Artigiano over suspicious transactions; IOR president Ettore Gotti Tedeschi and another senior official placed under investigation; Vatican said it was 'perplexed and astonished' and backed Gotti Tedeschi

Funds released 31 May/June 2011; Gotti Tedeschi ousted 24 May 2012; his laundering case dropped July 2013; October 2013 about 1,300 lay customers asked to close accounts; Promontory review from May 2013; Cipriani and Tulliò convicted February 2017 of omissions (4 months 10 days), acquitted of laundering

Nunzio Scarano, senior APSA accountant for 22 years, charged June 2013 with plotting with a secret-service agent and a broker to bring 20m euros into Italy from Switzerland; the IOR froze over 2m euros in 10 accounts; January 2016 Rome court acquitted him of corruption and attempted smuggling, convicted him of false accusation (two years suspended); separate Salerno laundering trial; he said his assets came from donations

Vatican tribunal, 21 January 2021: Angelo Caloia (IOR president 1989-2009) and lawyer Gabriele Liuzzo sentenced to 8 years 11 months and 12,500 euro fines for embezzlement and self-laundering; Lamberto Liuzzo 5 years 2 months for laundering; 29 properties of IOR and SGIR sold below value 2002-2007; court found about 19m euros appropriated; about 38m euros confiscation and over 20m euros damages; first application of December 2018 law per the Press Office
Defendants maintained their innocence and sought to call former secretaries of state and cardinals to show the sales were approved; Caloia was 81, Gabriele Liuzzo 97

vt10_london.topic: The London property case: investment, sale, trial, verdict, appeal, retrial status as of October 2026

claims.text: 24 September 2020: the Pope accepted Becciu's resignation as Prefect of the Congregation for the Causes of Saints and 'from the rights connected with the Cardinalate'

Verdict 16 December 2023 after 86 hearings, Tribunal president Giuseppe Pignatone; ten defendants and four companies; Becciu 5 years 6 months, 8,000 euro fine, perpetual disqualification for three counts of embezzlement (Athena payment, Marogna payments, 125,000 euros to Caritas Ozieri for SPES cooperative chaired by his brother); acquitted of other charges; Mincione 5y6m; Torzi 6 years (aggravated fraud, extortion, self-laundering); Crasso 7y; Tirabassi 7y; Squillace 1y10m suspended; Marogna 3y9m; Brülhart and Di Ruzza 1,750 euro fines; Carlino acquitted; embezzlement over $200.5m paid 2013-2014 for shares in Mincione-linked Athena fund, 'about one-third of the availability at the time'; Marogna over 570,000 euros

AP: tribunal ordered 166m euros confiscated and 200m euros civil damages; prosecutors had sought over 400m euros; Becciu first cardinal prosecuted by the Vatican court; lawyer Viglione said he respected the sentence but would appeal; Diddi said the outcome 'showed we were correct'; defence said procedural norms gave prosecutors 'enormous leeway to withhold evidence'; Becciu said the 125,000 euros went to a bakery for at-risk youths and stayed in diocesan coffers; Torzi defence: negotiated exit, not extortion

1 July 2022: Vatican finalised sale of 60 Sloane Avenue to Bain Capital for 186m pounds (215m euros); Secretariat of State put about 350m euros into the building; prosecutors estimated losses over 200m euros; losses absorbed by Secretariat reserves, not Peter's Pence

Appeal opened 22 September 2025 before Court of Appeal presided by Alejandro Arellano Cedillo, Dean of the Roman Rota; Becciu claims 'absolute innocence'; defence sought chats between Chaouqui, Perlasca and Ciferri omitted at first instance

17 March 2026: Court of Appeal ordered a partial mistrial; procedural errors nullified the original indictment and required renewal; trial and judgment keep effects for acquitted defendants without valid appeal; papal Rescripts reaffirmed as legitimate but lack of timely publication of one 'may have affected the validity' of some measures; ECHR arguments not upheld; Promoter to deposit full acts by 30 April, parties by 15 June, hearing 22 June 2026

AP 17 March 2026: 16-page ruling; prosecutors' failure to give the defence all evidence nullified the indictment; unpublished papal decree ineffective; in January 2026 Cassation upheld dismissal of the prosecutor's appeal for a procedural error and Diddi stepped aside; Tirabassi's lawyers: first time a papal rescript ruled invalid; Torzi held 10 days June 2020 without warrant
CWR/EWTN and ANSA: ruling of 'relative nullity' does not overturn the first-instance verdicts, which keep legal effect for now; Becciu: 'my complete innocence will be recognized soon'

Avvenire: Court declined to annul the whole first-instance trial ('non dichiara la nullità complessiva'); renewal of hearings before the Court of Appeal itself; the citation to trial was vitiated by incomplete filing with omissis; Becciu calls the case 'una macchinazione ai miei danni'
30 April 2026: Promoter of Justice's office did not deposit the complete records by the deadline, according to defence lawyers Viglione and Marzo
Status as of 19 September 2026: defence briefs due 21 September; hearing set for 29 October 2026; Viglione said the defence is 'at peace'

Becciu was Substitute for General Affairs 2011-2018 (term ended 29 June 2018); indicted 3 July 2021; trial opened 27 July 2021; he said he was 'the victim of a plot' and that Francis authorised a ransom of up to $1m for a kidnapped Colombian nun; in 2023 prosecutors introduced letters in which Francis denied authorising the hiring of Marogna or the London investment; on 29 April 2025 he said he would not take part in the conclave 'for the good of the church'

vt10_reform.topic: Reform after the scandals: IOR clean-up 2013-15, centralisation of funds 2020-22

claims.text: IOR 2014 report (ANSA): 2,600 inactive accounts closed May 2013 to 31 December 2014; 554 closed as not fitting the client profile; 1,460 closed on natural termination; 274 more being closed; 15,181 clients at end-2014; profit 69.3m euros in 2014 vs 2.9m in 2013; de Franssu: 'great commitment in dealing with offenses that in past have affected the Institute'

AIF 2015 report: about 4,800 accounts closed after the IOR's revision, completed in October, as 'no longer in compliance with the Vatican regulatory framework' by nationality, residence or use of funds

Rescript of 23 August 2022: Holy See and connected entities, including the Secretariat of State, to move financial and liquid assets held in other banks to the IOR within 30 days of 1 September 2022; asset management and custody of the Holy See's movable patrimony is 'the exclusive responsibility' of the IOR under Praedicate Evangelium art. 219 §3; the Secretariat had held accounts at Swiss banks incl. Credit Suisse through which the London investment was first made
